decision.root_cause_hypothesis: The quality_score scorer is producing mis-scaled or overflowed outputs (many values far outside the documented [0,1] range), indicating an implementation/scoring bug rather than optimizer or planning issues.
decision.rationale: Run diagnostics show quality_score max=485,165,195.40979, mean=457,634,869.840732, and 31/32 values outside the declared [0,1] range; this numeric domination will swamp parameter_spread (mean=0.343545, std=0.039064) despite its weight=0.3. Temporarily dropping the faulty objective stops the optimizer from optimizing an artefact and allows continued progress on the plausible parameter_spread signal.
decision.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Prevents the optimizer from being driven by bogus large quality_score values so that it can meaningfully optimize parameter_spread (currently mean=0.343545, best=0.401328). Should restore sensible selection pressure and let useful improvements (e.g., higher parameter_spread) appear.
decision.validation_plan_suggested_by_judge: Run iteration 2 with quality_score removed and check that the optimizer progresses on parameter_spread: expect no out-of-range objective dominance, and preferably an increased best or mean parameter_spread relative to iteration 1 (best 0.401328, mean 0.343545). Also monitor population diversity to ensure search doesn't collapse.

target_assessment.objective: Dropping the faulty objective is the fastest, lowest-risk way to stop numerical domination and resume useful optimization of parameter_spread.
target_assessment.planning: Changing planner guidance alone won't stop numeric domination by bad scores and is unlikely to produce an immediate improvement detectable by the validator.
target_assessment.implementation: Sanitizing or rebuilding the scorer would directly fix the root cause but requires developer work; sanitize_outputs could mark out-of-range values as failed which might harm selection—still credible but riskier than temporarily dropping the objective.
target_assessment.optimization_workflow: Tuning optimizer params won't fix the underlying bad scores; it only adjusts search behavior against a corrupted objective.
target_assessment.no_change: Leaving the state unchanged will let the huge, incorrect quality_score values continue to dominate and likely waste budget on artefacts.

decision.root_cause_hypothesis: The quality_score scorer is mis-scaled or mis-implemented and is producing values orders of magnitude above its declared [0,1] range (evidence: min=432901163.458318, mean=483531944.411307, n_outside_declared_range=32); I'm reasonably confident but not certain without inspecting the scorer code.
decision.rationale: All 32 quality_score values are outside the declared [0,1] range (min=432,901,163; mean=483,531,944; std=9,093,556), so this objective can dominate or mislead selection. Meanwhile parameter_spread (mean=0.418782, std=0.014226) and parameter_mean (mean=0.56166, std=0.027239) are within expected ranges and showing consistent, meaningful improvement. Dropping the faulty quality_score objective immediately removes the risk of misdirected search and lets trusted objectives drive iteration 3.
decision.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Removal will prevent the mis-scaled quality_score from distorting selection/ranking, allowing parameter_spread and parameter_mean (both trusted and improving: spread mean≈0.4188 improved +0.0752, mean≈0.5617 improved −0.0849) to guide optimization and thus produce more meaningful next-iteration progress.
decision.validation_plan_suggested_by_judge: Run the next iteration with quality_score removed and check that the optimizer shows continued or improved progress on the trusted objectives (e.g., parameter_spread best > 0.448496 or parameter_mean best < 0.519361, or net improvement in the accepted multi-objective metric computed without quality_score). The independent validator will compare the new state to the currently accepted state; success is improvement in the optimizer's validated metric(s) when the misleading objective is absent.

target_assessment.objective: High-value target: the evidence (all 32 quality_score values outside [0,1], huge magnitudes) directly implicates the objective and dropping it is a minimal, reversible fix.
target_assessment.planning: Less direct: changing planner guidance could help future objective choices but won't stop the immediate damage from a mis-scaled scorer.
target_assessment.implementation: Plausible: sanitizing or rebinding the quality_score scorer could fix the root cause, but requires knowing which scorer variant is correct — drop is faster and lower-risk now.
target_assessment.optimization_workflow: Unlikely to help: tuning mutation/crossover etc. won't correct selection bias caused by a mis-scaled objective.
target_assessment.no_change: Risky: leaving the mis-scaled objective in place is likely to continue misleading the search and waste iterations.
